# THE PROGRAM
### Regeneron STS 2027 · rutile-MO₂(110) OER · execution plan 2026-08-09 → 2026-10-15

---

## 0. Two adjudications that reshape everything below

**Compute is free; attention is not.** 270 human hours over nine weeks, minus the report. The dossier's nine lanes sum to ~6,000–7,000 pw.x invocations against a lifetime archive of 153 `.out` files in 12 run directories. **Hard budget: ~700 DFT jobs, ~130 human hours on compute, ~140 hours on everything else (experiment, compliance, figures, writing prep).** Every item below is costed against that ceiling, and §5 names what is cut.

**Do not run A→B→C as a sequence.** Six of the nine lanes proposed six mutually incompatible dependency graphs over the same seven stages. All of them are trying to solve the same identification problem — the symmetry trap, the magnetic basin, the periodic image and the coverage are collinear in every observable currently in hand (docs/41 §2e: repeating the 1×1-vs-2×1 experiment *with* orientational starts collapses Ir's lateral term from +0.382 to +0.007 eV). **Cross them in one design. Do not stage them.** Critique 1 is right and it is the single most important structural correction in the whole packet.

---

## 1. THE LEAD CONTRIBUTION

### Honest working title

> **Three convergence-invisible error classes in computed OER overpotentials: a pre-registered audit of a seven-metal rutile MO₂(110) benchmark tier**

That is the title of the paper. The STS report gets a plainer one; the science is identical.

### The claim

For rutile MO₂(110) at the field-standard PBE+U / CHE protocol, **the computed overpotential is not reproducible from its own protocol.** Three error classes —

1. adsorbate relaxation confined to a slab mirror plane,
2. a path-dependent magnetic SCF solution carried through an entire relaxation,
3. a Hubbard *U* imported from an external calibration rather than computed,

— each move η by **more than the 0.772 V range the tier is used to discriminate**, and **none is detectable by any force, energy, k-point, cutoff, vacuum, dipole or slab-thickness convergence test.** We quantify all three across the full tier, *prove* the first with a Hessian, *measure the rate* of the second, *bracket* the third, and attach the first calibrated interval to η — which is wide enough that the original ranking is unresolved.

### Why this and not the alternatives

- **Not "we found a better catalyst."** The headline is withdrawn and P7 is why. Rebuilding a winner in nine weeks on a Hamiltonian you cannot yet defend is how you earn a third withdrawal.
- **Not "η is a biased estimator."** Deshpande/Kitchin/Viswanathan, *ACS Catal.* **6**, 5251 (2016) define exactly E[U_L] − U_L. Dead as a headline (§6).
- **Not "MLIPs fail on this tier."** Falsified by the project's own pre-registered docs/39 (`omat` ρ = +0.964, p = 0.0028). Repeating it breaks a pre-registration.
- **Not the HEA screen.** Tu *et al.*, *Sci. Adv.* **12**, eaed8479 (2026) published an ML-screened HEO OER catalyst with a PEMWE device this year.
- **Not the symmetry trap alone.** Goniakowski & Gillan, *Surf. Sci.* (1995) already say, on rutile TiO₂(110)/SnO₂(110), that "the symmetrical molecularly adsorbed configuration is unstable with respect to lowering of symmetry." Thirty-one years old on this exact surface family.

What survives is the **unification plus the closure argument**. The campaign has already eliminated six alternative explanations *by direct DFT* — gas references (algebraic), vacuum (−0.0005 V), dipole (−0.0018 V), thickness/constraint (+0.05 V, wrong sign), spin (wrong way), RPBE (+0.216 V, wrong way). That elimination is what turns three anecdotes into a diagnosis, and **it is U-invariant and permanent**: Ru and Ir carry U = 0 and nspin = 1, so no later stage can take it back. Nobody has audited these three classes together across a benchmark tier with a proof per state. That is the paper.

### The evidence that closes it

| element of the claim | closing evidence | status |
|---|---|---|
| the trap is exact, not approximate | max\|F_y\| = **0.0000000000** Ry/au on every adsorbate atom over all 243 ionic steps checked, while other atoms carry up to 0.049 | **in hand** |
| the trapped geometry is not a minimum | imaginary out-of-plane mode in the adsorbate partial Hessian at each on-record geometry; real spectrum at the escaped one | **W2–W6** |
| the basin failure is real and has a rate | GATE-1 fresh-density SCF at each final geometry: 5 of 18 states audited so far are multistable, drifts 59–405 meV | **in hand, extend to 28/28** |
| U is load-bearing | P7 triggered: η(Cr) moves **1.122 V** against a pre-registered 0.15 V threshold; production U placed Cr's descriptor at 1.560 eV, essentially on Man's 1.60 apex | **in hand** |
| nothing else explains it | six causes closed by direct DFT | **in hand** |
| the corrected tier cannot resolve its own ranking | Δ₉₅ = 1.645·sd(η_i − η_j) from paired BEEF ensembles | **W7** |

### The single figure

**Figure 1, two panels, one page.**

- **Panel A — the waterfall.** Seven columns, one per metal. Each starts at the tier-of-record η and steps down/up through four measured corrections in fixed order: *cell/periodic image* → *mirror-plane escape* → *magnetic ground state* → *U bracket* (as a shaded band, not a step). Terminal point carries the calibrated interval. Two annotations: the tier's original 0.772 V total spread drawn as a horizontal reference bar, and the biggest single correction drawn against it.
- **Panel B — what survives.** The corrected tier as a **partial order with explicit ties**, ties drawn as shaded bands of width Δ₉₅, with the original strict ranking ghosted behind it.

Panel A says *the corrections are bigger than the signal*. Panel B says *and here is the honest ordering that remains*. A referee gets the whole thesis in ten seconds and can verify Panel A's first row against the raw outputs in five minutes.

## 2. SUPPORTING CONTRIBUTIONS, RANKED

**S1 — The scaling-floor decomposition.** Because ΔG₂ + ΔG₃ ≡ c_M = ΔG_OOH − ΔG_OH once 4.92 eV is imposed, **η ≥ c_M/2 − 1.23 exactly.** Applied to data already on disk: Ir at c = 3.652 has floor 0.596 V against reported 0.781 (excess 0.185); off-plane Ir at c = 3.361 has floor 0.451 against 0.490 (excess **0.039** — already *on* its floor). Cr (0.491) and Co (0.544) both sit *below* Ir's floor, which back-solves to c_Cr ≲ 3.44, c_Co ≲ 3.55 — i.e. **the withdrawn Cr headline was scaling-limited, not descriptor-limited.** This is the best unexploited result in the entire dossier, it costs zero compute, and it explains *why* P7 bit. Zero lanes contradicted it.
*Carrying object:* Table — per metal, c_M, floor, excess, and z-score against Divanis 2020's pooled 3.18 ± 0.12 eV. Add the z-score column to every corrected tier as a pre-registered acceptance gate: a correction that moves η but leaves c_M at +3.9σ has not fixed anything.

**S2 — First-principles Hubbard parameters for rutile OER surfaces.** DFPT (hp.x) U for all seven metals **including Ru and Ir**, both projectors, reported as a **bracket** with the ranking-stability statistic — never as a replacement U. No published linear-response U exists for rutile FeO₂/CoO₂/NiO₂, and arXiv full-text returns zero DFPT-U calculations on any catalytic slab. The internal inconsistency it fixes (U on 3d because Materials Project publishes numbers, U = 0 on 4d/5d because it does not) is the fastest thing a DFT-literate judge will find.
*Carrying object:* Figure — η_i(U_i) over 0–9 eV, seven curves, four independently-derived U values marked (MP-fitted, DFPT-atomic, DFPT-ortho-atomic, Xu supercell-LR from the CC0 Zenodo data), plus Spearman ρ(tier@U_MP, tier@U_DFPT) with exact permutation p.

**S3 — The *OOH corpus hole.** Three independent strands already agree: Karimitari *et al.* (arXiv:2605.09394) report fine-tuned models reach <0.1 eV on O*/OH* but "still struggle predicting the OOH* step, indicating that the OOH* step is highly under-represented"; the project's own OC22 audit found **1 rutile system with *OOH out of 62,331**, and **zero** among the 19 rutile(110) systems touching these metals; and both MACE and UMA-`omat` desorb *OOH on the 3d metals against a DFT ground truth of 2.08–2.55 Å. Nobody has put the corpus audit and the model behaviour in the same figure.
*Carrying object:* Figure — predicted vs DFT M–O distance for *OOH, five model families × 7+ metals, 3.00 Å desorption cut drawn, DFT ground truth overlaid; inset table of *OOH-on-rutile(110) counts per public corpus.

**S4 — The component-resolved error budget and the resolution number.** One row per source (XC from BEEF, U from the hp.x/P7 bracket, magnetic solution from the GATE-1 spread, adsorbate configuration from multi-start, cell/coverage, numerics), each with a measured 1σ, a note on how it was measured, and a common-mode flag. Then Δ₉₅ and the P(η_i < η_j) matrix.
*Carrying object:* Table (budget) + heatmap (pairwise probability). **The abstract sentence:** *"The tier resolves η differences larger than X V at 95% posterior probability; within that window we report ranks as unresolved."*

**S5 — The estimator identity, as a supporting section.** η = max(ΔG_i) − mean(ΔG_i) whenever the four rungs are constrained to 4.92 eV; bias ≥ 0 by Jensen with equality iff the argmax is deterministic; and — the one part I could not find published — **the bias is governed by (top-two ΔG gap)/(error scale), not by η.** Cite Deshpande 2016 and Chatterjee *et al.* (arXiv:2512.05938) in the same sentence.
*Carrying object:* Small figure — bias contour over (gap, σ) at the measured ρ, with each of the seven metals plotted as a point. **Do not quote 0.73–0.78 V as "the bias"**; at the ρ ≈ 0.85–0.95 the BEEF ensemble will almost certainly measure, it is +0.02 to +0.07 V.

**S6 — The experimental module.** Not a validation of the tier. A **pre-registered null**: the computed bulk-composition ranking does not survive contact with a reconstructing electrode, and here is the surface it converges to.
*Carrying object:* Figure — measured η₁₀ vs **post-OER surface Ni:Fe from XPS/Raman**, points coloured by nominal bulk composition. If that plot has structure and the nominal-composition plot does not, that is the result.

**S7 — MLIP re-benchmark against the corrected tier,** with the degradation pre-registered before Stage A runs. MACE-MPA-0 trains on MPtrj at exactly the MP U set with U = 0 on Ru/Ir — the identical partition this campaign uses. The current ρ is confounded with a shared Hubbard convention.
*Carrying object:* Table — ρ, exact p, η MAE, descriptor MAE and c_M MAE for five model families against tier_v1 and tier_v2, with the pre-registration DOI in the caption.

### WEEKS 3–5 · Aug 24 – Sep 13 — ★ THE CORE SWEEP (the critical path)

**One crossed design, not three stages.** For all seven metals × four states, in the frozen production cell:

- **Orientation multi-start**, off-plane, with `nosym=.true. noinv=.true.` **and a physical displacement** (nosym alone does nothing when the input is exactly symmetric — F_y stays ~1e-8 against a 1e-3 threshold). Grid: clean ×1, *O ×2, *OH ×3, *OOH ×4, **plus the two bridge-protonated isomers as mandatory members** (−OO···H−O_br and O-on-cus/H-on-O_br). Generate and pre-rank the grid with MACE-MPA-0 **and** UMA-`omat` independently, take the **union** of distinct basins, confirm top-k in DFT. Models as *generators*, never as rankers — this removes the circularity Lane C could not answer.
- **Magnetic multi-start**: 2 initialisations per state for the five 3d metals (high/low |m₀| × sign pattern, split the metal into per-atom ATOMIC_SPECIES with identical U).
- **GATE-1 on every final geometry**: fresh-density fixed-geometry SCF; if it lands lower, re-relax from that solution and repeat until GATE-1 passes. This is the campaign's own machinery and it has already caught 5 multistable states.
- **Legacy 1×1 arm** run identically so the cell delta is *measured*, not assumed.
- **Path-independence control**: the external optimizer on Cr, Co, Ir only (12 relaxations). You do not need path-independence everywhere; you need it *demonstrated once* and the GATE-1 loop everywhere.

| item | jobs | compute |
|---|---|---|
| Production-cell sweep | ~120 relaxations (36-atom) | ~10 box-days on 12 boxes |
| Legacy 1×1 arm | ~120 relaxations (18-atom) | ~4 box-days on 8 boxes |
| GATE-1 SCFs | ~240 SCFs | ~1 box-day |
| Re-relax loop (~30% failure) | ~40 relaxations | ~3 box-days |
| Path-independence control | 12 relaxations | ~2 box-days |
| **Total** | **~290 relax + 240 SCF** | **~4 days wall on 25–30 parallel boxes; budget 3 weeks for triage** |

**Running concurrently, separate box sets, off the critical path:**

- **3X — U-free tier expansion.** Ti, Sn, Nb, V, Pb (+ Ge/Mo if cheap). No U decision, no magnetic search, so no dependency on anything. 5 metals × 4 states × ~4 starts = **80 relaxations**, ~4 box-days. **Commit MLIP predictions to git before each launch** — this converts the project's zero held-out points into a genuine pre-registered test and is the single largest defensibility upgrade available. Pick for *spread* in η, not count; target n = 12.
- **3Y — Clean-slab site-resolved hp.x** on **two** metals only (Cr, Ru), `find_atpert=1`, plus the slab-thickness convergence check on one. Lane B is right against Lane A here: 7 metals × 4 adsorbates × 3 iterations is out of reach. **U is fixed per metal across its four rungs** and that approximation is stated — recomputing U per adsorbate makes the four CHE rungs non-comparable anyway.
- **3Z — Experiment.** Purify KOH (Trotochaud protocol, ~4 h bench). **Pilot on one composition and measure the replicate SD.** Every power number depends on it being ~15 mV; if it is 30 mV, re-plan *now*.

**Uniformity rule — the most important line in the program.** η is built from differences against the clean slab. Auditing *OOH deeply and the clean slab shallowly injects a *new* systematic of unpredictable sign. Co's +59 meV clean-slab drift is proof the reference is not safe. **Declare an audit depth per metal and apply it identically to all four states, including the ones you expect to be clean. Publish the per-state depth table. Holes are reported as holes.**

## 4. FREEZE CHECKPOINTS

Assume at least one stage fails. Each checkpoint has a **minimum viable result that is already a defensible paper.**

### CP1 — Sunday Aug 23
**Stop and assess.** Cell decided; Hessian pilot returned; hp.x TiO₂ verdict in.
**MVR if everything downstream fails:** *the audit as it already stands.*
1. The anchor deficit closed by elimination — six causes killed by direct DFT, Ir explained as a basin failure (3.652 → 3.361, η 0.781 → 0.490, inside the published band), Ru shown to be the field's published systematic (Liang 2022, same pls = 3 signature) rather than a defect.
2. P7 triggered at 1.122 V against 0.15 V, with the mechanism: production U placed Cr on the volcano apex.
3. The multistability rate: every magnetic 3d endmember except Mn carries ≥1 multistable state; both nspin = 1 anchors carry none.
4. The symmetry trap with max\|F_y\| = 0.0000000000 and the Ir demonstration.
5. The estimator identity and the resolution number.

**That is a complete, honest, publishable STS report and it exists today.** Build the report skeleton around exactly it in Week 1, so every later result slots into a slot that already exists.

*Failure branches:* hp.x cannot reproduce TiO₂ ≈ 4.9 eV → **ship A0 only** (η(U) grid + bracket from MP/Xu/literature), state hp.x was attempted and did not validate. Hessian pilot shows no imaginary mode → the lead contribution loses its proof; reweight to S1 (scaling floor) + S4 (error budget) as the lead, and report the symmetry effect as an energy measurement without the saddle-point claim.

### CP2 — Sunday Sep 13
**Core sweep drained or cut.**
**MVR:** the corrected tier at **one** cell with symmetry and magnetism fixed to a uniform declared depth, U as a *sensitivity band only*. If the 2×1 arm did not finish, report the 1×1 tier with the 3-metal cell pilot as the measured cell correction and say so.
*Trigger to cut:* if by Sep 8 fewer than 60% of the production-cell relaxations have cleared GATE-1, kill the legacy 1×1 arm and reallocate.

### CP3 — Saturday Oct 4
**Uncertainty and MLIP in or out.**
**MVR:** everything above, with the error budget's U row populated from the **P7 bracket** rather than hp.x, and the XC row from the anchors' BEEF ensembles transferred to the 3d metals with the transfer assumption stated. If BEEF fails, quote the U-bracket width and the GATE-1 drift distribution as an explicitly non-Gaussian range and say it is a lower bound.

### CP4 — Wednesday Oct 15 — HARD FREEZE
No exceptions, no "one more run." Any stage not complete is reported as **scoped-but-not-run**, which is a legitimate publishable sentence and costs far less than a half-finished stage.

## 5. KILL LIST

**Killed by the critics, correctly:**

| item | why |
|---|---|
| **Fine-tuning MACE-MPA-0** | Karimitari Table 5: 2,208 configs → 0.305 eV vs 49,860 → 0.277 eV. The project has 896 frames, all generated with F_y ≡ 0 — literally zero data on the coordinate the search must explore — labelled at a U about to be replaced, and it would be scored on the seven points that trained it. Lane G was right against Lanes C and E. Use foundation models as *generators*. |
| **The NiOOH/FeOOH oxyhydroxide tier** | The proposed fix for the U problem is a new material with a *worse* U problem (Ni³⁺ Jahn-Teller, proton-ordering ambiguity), plus an edge-site model decision, plus its own magnetic search, started in the last weeks with no pipeline validation. ~200 relaxations for a second unvalidated campaign. |
| **The SQS rutile-HEA tier** | Models a phase that does not exist on the electrode. |
| **OSCDFT Tier 3** | Source rebuild + regression suite + 400–800 constrained SCFs + recursive intersection search, and it forces a second pw.x binary in a campaign whose entire thesis is protocol consistency. Tiers 0–2 plus the GATE-1 loop are sufficient. |
| **Environ** | docs/42 (run on the box, 2026-08-09): Environ NOT INSTALLED, but ESM and 3D-RISM **already compiled** and blocked only by missing `.MOL` data. Lane D proposed the expensive route and a second QE 7.2/7.3 environment when the cheap one was already found in-house. |
| **Lane E's "BEEF-vdW is a dead end"** | Logical error — absence of a CMake `OPTION` is consistent with unconditional compilation, which is what it is (`qe_libbeef`, guarded only by `#if !defined(__NOBEEF)`). docs/42 records the literal banner `Initializing libbeef V0.1.2`. **Re-check every DEAD END in the dossier against docs/42; at least one is demonstrably wrong.** |
| **The 300–600-relaxation η(U) grid** | Mis-costed by ~20× once every point became a multi-start ensemble in a 36-atom cell. Replaced by 140 fixed-geometry SCFs. |
| **hp.x on adsorbate-covered slabs, 7×4×3** | Lane B right against Lane A. Bulk for seven, clean-slab site-resolved for two, U fixed per metal across rungs, approximation stated. |
| **Claiming exhaustive collinear enumeration** | True at 1×1 (2⁶ = 64 → 32). Dies at 2×1 (2¹² = 4,096). Report instead "enumerated N orderings under a stated protocol until two rounds produced no new solution," with the discovery curve plotted. |
| **The A→B→C sequence** | Six lanes, six incompatible dependency graphs. One crossed design. |

**Killed on time-cost, all correctly flagged by the lanes themselves and still occupying planning space:** explicit-water AIMD (1–2 box-weeks per trajectory, and Di Liberto needed a national allocation and still called their sampling inadequate); ESM-RISM and grand-canonical DFT (incomparable to the Man volcano, week+ learning); hybrids (no EXX forces with US/PAW in QE ⇒ full pseudopotential revalidation); r2SCAN (conda-forge QE has no libxc; NLCC inconsistency); ACBN0/PAOFLOW/AFLOWpi; U+V *production* (harvest V from the same hp.x runs and report it as a table — that alone is new for FeO₂/CoO₂/NiO₂ — but do not convert the tier); AiiDA (PostgreSQL + RabbitMQ, a classic nine-week sink; write the 60-line driver); RomeoDFT.jl; GOFEE/AIRSS/GOCIA/CatKit/ACAT; pymatgen `MagneticStructureEnumerator`; a self-hosted leaderboard; JOSS; a Digital Discovery resubmission of the combined story (its published desk-reject list names "electronic structure method comparisons without machine learning").

**Killed on scope, my call:** the purified-vs-as-received KOH contrast arm (cheapest genuinely novel experiment available, but it doubles electrochemistry hours — run purified only, and note the contrast as future work); 12 compositions × 4 replicates (cut to 6 × 3, contrast-first); ICP-OES if access is not already confirmed.

**Do NOT kill, despite the temptation:** the GATE-1 fresh-density SCF on every state. It has already caught five real failures including a 405 meV one and a contaminated clean-slab reference. It is the cheapest high-yield gate in the campaign.

## 6. NOVELTY LEDGER

| claim | verdict | prior art that decided it | narrowed wording |
|---|---|---|---|
| **η = max − mean is a positively biased estimator, in closed form; no prior art** | **DEAD as stated** | Deshpande, Kitchin & Viswanathan, *ACS Catal.* **6**, 5251 (2016) define U_EL and use E[U_L] − U_L as a predictability diagnostic. Krishnamurthy/Sumaria/Viswanathan JPCL **9**, 588 (2018) generalise. Chatterjee/Bengio/Rolnick/Therrien arXiv:2512.05938 (Dec 2025) at the same 0.3–0.5 eV σ. Calle-Vallejo JPCC (2025) derives the η–ESSI causal relation. And 1.23 = 4.92/4 is arithmetic. | *"Deshpande et al. showed for ORR that the limiting potential is upward-biased; we give the closed-form identity for OER, prove bias ≥ 0 by Jensen with equality iff the argmax is deterministic, and show the bias is governed by (top-two ΔG gap)/(error scale) rather than by η."* Only the last clause is unfound. |
| **An MLIP repeatedly caught errors in its own DFT reference** | **DEAD** | AdsorbML (arXiv:2211.16486, npj Comput. Mater. **9**, 172) Table 3: ML+RX finds minima >0.1 eV below the DFT baseline **9.10–18.71%** of the time; "ML models found much better minima between 5%–15% of the time." Beating DFT is *designed into* their success criterion. 4/21 = 19% sits at the ceiling of a published band. | *"MLIP-guided restarts corrected 4 of 21 states (19%), at the top of the 9–19% AdsorbML ML+RX base rate."* **Then pivot to what is new:** at n = 7, one MLIP-seeded basin (Cr *O) carries the entire statistical significance of both models — reverting it takes MACE from p = 0.0238 to 0.8397 and `omat` from 0.0028 to 0.3024. That is a real, unpublished warning about small-n MLIP benchmarks. Keep the 9 meV Cr anecdote as colour. |
| **The mirror-plane symmetry trap as a newly identified error class** | **DEAD as discovery; SURVIVES as a quantified audit** | Goniakowski & Gillan, *Surf. Sci.* (1995), on rutile TiO₂(110) **and SnO₂(110)**: "allowance is made for relaxation of the adsorbed species to unsymmetrical configurations"; "the symmetrical molecularly adsorbed configuration is unstable with respect to lowering of symmetry." Sun/Reuter/Scheffler PRB **70**, 235402 (2004) call it "crucial" on RuO₂(110). VASP ISYM wiki; OC20/AdsorbML randomise orientation by construction. | *"The precaution has been known on rutile(110) since at least 1995 and was called crucial in 2004, yet it is invisible to every standard convergence criterion and its cost across an OER benchmark tier has never been audited, nor has the constrained geometry ever been shown to be a saddle point."* **The load-bearing novel object is the Hessian proof**, for which I found no precedent on these states. |
| **A tier-wide SCF-multiplicity audit with a reported rate** | **SURVIVES, narrowed** | Named since Dorado (2009); Meredig PRB **82**, 195218 (2010); Allen & Watson PCCP **16**, 21016 (2014); Keshavarz & Thunström arXiv:1810.10393; Ponet/Di Lucente/Marzari npj Comput. Mater. **10**, 151 (2024) count 50+ solutions for Ni₂O₂ at U = 6 eV; Horton *et al.* npj Comput. Mater. **5**, 64 (2019) report a ~40% ordering-failure rate on 64 bulk magnets **using the exact U set this campaign uses.** No surface/adsorption rate exists. | *"The multiplicity of self-consistent DFT+U solutions is well established in bulk correlated oxides [Allen & Watson; Meredig; Ponet]. We quantify it, for the first time to our knowledge, across an OER adsorption benchmark tier, and propagate it into η."* **Report a COUNT with a Wilson CI and the meV distribution — never a bare percentage.** At n = 28 the interval is ±18 points and a bare "19%" is indistinguishable from AdsorbML's 9–19% or Horton's 40%. |
| **DFPT (hp.x) Hubbard parameters for a rutile OER slab; first linear-response U for rutile FeO₂/CoO₂/NiO₂** | **SURVIVES** | arXiv full-text returns literally zero DFPT/hp.x Hubbard-U calculations on any catalytic slab, across three query formulations. FeO₂/CoO₂/NiO₂ are absent from the Xu/Kitchin CC0 dataset and from every other source checked. | As stated, with "to our knowledge" and the caveat that no protocol exists to copy beyond QE's own 2D examples 08/09. |
| **No foundation MLIP has an externally anchored OER error bar** | **SURVIVES, heavily narrowed** | No MLIP paper reports error against *measured* OER overpotentials. But the broad form is near-tautological (MLIPs are trained on DFT labels) and false at the DFT level (Man 2011 anchored computed to measured overpotentials — that is where this campaign's volcano comes from). Nearest external adsorption anchor: Wellendorff *et al.*, *Surf. Sci.* **640**, 36 (2015) — transition-metal surfaces, not oxides. | *"We report the first comparison of an MLIP-predicted OER overpotential against an overpotential we measured ourselves under a stated, pre-registered protocol, at n = N."* **Never write "first externally anchored" without n immediately after.** At n ≤ 3 the words "calibrated" and "externally anchored" must not appear in the same sentence. |
| **The *OOH corpus hole paired with universal model behaviour** | **SURVIVES** | Karimitari arXiv:2605.09394 §4.2.2 states the under-representation; the project's OC22 audit measures it (1 of 62,331); no one has published the corpus audit and the model behaviour together for rutile(110). | As stated. |

Sci.* **11**, 2943 supplies the pooled 3.18 ± 0.12 eV calibration. | Present as a lemma and a per-metal diagnostic table, not as a finding. Its value is that it converts the failed anchor gate into a quantitative diagnosis at zero compute. |
